s: Hannah prays in the temple for a son, and God gives her Samuel, whom she dedicates to the Lord.
Hannah sings her song of praise. Eli's sons are wicked, and a man of God warns Eli.
God calls the boy Samuel in the night, and Samuel answers, Speak, Lord, for your servant hears.
The Philistines capture the ark. Eli's sons die, and Eli dies at the news.
The ark brings disaster on the Philistines and their god Dagon falls before it.
The Philistines send the ark back on a cart.
Samuel calls Israel to repentance, and God gives victory at Mizpah.
The people ask for a king like other nations. Samuel warns them what a king will take.
Saul is searching for lost donkeys when he meets Samuel.
Samuel anoints Saul as king, and he is chosen by lot.
Saul rescues Jabesh-gilead from the Ammonites and is confirmed as king.
Samuel's farewell speech: fear the Lord and serve him faithfully.
Saul offers sacrifice himself instead of waiting for Samuel, and is told his kingdom will not last.
Jonathan attacks the Philistines with his armour-bearer, and God gives a great victory. Saul's rash oath almost costs Jonathan's life.
Saul disobeys God's command concerning Amalek. Samuel tells him that to obey is better than sacrifice, and God rejects him as king.
Samuel anoints the young shepherd David. David plays the harp to soothe Saul.
David kills the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone, trusting in the Lord.
Jonathan loves David as himself. Saul grows jealous of David's success and tries to kill him.
Saul keeps trying to kill David, who escapes with help from Michal and Jonathan.
Jonathan warns David to flee, and the two friends part in tears.
David flees and is given the holy bread by the priest at Nob.
David gathers men at the cave of Adullam. Saul has the priests of Nob killed.
David saves the town of Keilah and keeps escaping Saul.
David spares Saul's life in a cave, cutting only the edge of his robe.
Samuel dies. Abigail prevents David from taking revenge on her foolish husband Nabal, and later becomes his wife.
David spares Saul a second time, taking only his spear and water jar.
David takes refuge among the Philistines.
Saul consults a medium at Endor, and Samuel's spirit foretells his death.
The Philistine lords send David away from their army.
David recovers his family and goods from the Amalekites who raided Ziklag.
Saul and Jonathan die in battle on Mount Gilboa.

3: The boy Samuel learns to listen for God's voice. He becomes the prophet who will anoint Israel's first kings.
8: The people want a king like other nations. God allows it, though he alone is their true king.
16: God chooses the youngest son, a shepherd boy, because God looks at the heart. The Messiah will come from David's line.
17: David defeats the giant not with armour but with trust in God.
